one_liner: Cloud data platform for warehousing, analytics, data sharing, and AI workloads.

evidence.claim: Snowflake REST APIs support OAuth, key-pair JWT, programmatic access tokens, and workload identity federation for authentication.
evidence.quote:
Using key pair authentication
*   [Using OAuth](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/snowflake-rest-api/authentication#label-sfrest-authenticating-oauth)
*   [Using a programmatic access token (PAT)]

evidence.claim: OAuth tokens are sent as bearer tokens in the Authorization header.
evidence.quote:
`Authorization: Bearer oauth_token`
where `oauth_token` is the generated OAuth token.

evidence.claim: Snowflake provides a public REST API (SQL API) that can run queries and manage deployment resources like users, roles, and tables.
evidence.quote:
The Snowflake SQL API is a REST API that you can use to access and update data in a Snowflake database. You can use this API to develop custom applications and integrations that:
*   Perform queries
*   Manage your deployment (e.g. provision users and roles, create tables, etc.)

evidence.claim: Snowflake itself ships and documents a managed MCP server for AI agents.
evidence.quote: The Snowflake-managed MCP server lets AI agents securely retrieve data from Snowflake accounts without needing to deploy separate infrastructure.

evidence.claim: API access is tied to a standard Snowflake user account via documented setup steps, with no partner program requirement mentioned.
evidence.quote: Assign the public key to your Snowflake user. After you assign the key to the user, run the [DESCRIBE USER](https://docs.snowflake.com/sql-reference/sql/desc-user) command.

notes: Vendor-managed MCP server is documented on docs.snowflake.com and requires OAuth; the older Snowflake-Labs/mcp community server on GitHub is explicitly 'no longer supported'. JWTs from key-pair auth are valid for at most one hour. Additional auth options include programmatic access tokens (PAT) and workload identity federation. The supplied material does not state trial/signup terms, so the access tier (free trial vs paid) is marked unknown, though API docs are fully public and self-serve for any account holder. SQL API effectively exposes unlimited breadth since any SQL statement (DDL/DML/admin) can be executed.
